directAnswer: Pope Innocent III was Lotario dei Conti di Segni, elected at about thirty-seven, who reigned from 1198 to 1216 and is widely seen as the most powerful of the medieval popes. He intervened in the politics of the empire, England and France, called the Fourth Crusade and the Albigensian Crusade, welcomed St. Francis and St. Dominic, and convened the Fourth Lateran Council in 1215.

sections.h2: Lotario of Segni, Theologian and Canonist
paras: Lotario was born around 1160 at Gavignano, near Segni, into the family of the counts of Segni. He studied theology at Paris and law at Bologna, and his uncle Clement III made him a cardinal deacon. During the reign of Celestine III he wrote several works, including the treatise On the Misery of the Human Condition, a meditation on human frailty that circulated widely.
Elected on January 8, 1198, the day Celestine died, he was then only about thirty-seven and still a deacon.

sections.h2: Kings, Emperors and the Vicar of Christ
paras: Innocent described the pope as the Vicar of Christ and compared papal and royal authority to the sun and the moon. In the disputed German election after Henry VI's death, his bull Venerabilem (1202) asserted the pope's right to examine the candidate he would crown as emperor. He also acted as guardian of the young Frederick II, Henry's heir in Sicily.

When King John of England refused to accept Stephen Langton as archbishop of Canterbury, Innocent placed England under interdict in 1208 and later excommunicated John. In 1213 John submitted and made England a papal fief. Innocent then sided with John against the barons and in 1215 annulled Magna Carta. He also pressed Philip II of France to take back his wife Ingeborg of Denmark.

sections.h2: The Fourth Crusade and the Albigensian Crusade
paras: Innocent proclaimed the Fourth Crusade in 1198. Indebted to Venice, the crusaders attacked the Christian city of Zara in 1202, and Innocent excommunicated them. In 1204 they sacked Constantinople. Innocent condemned the atrocities, though he accepted the Latin Empire that resulted, and the sack deepened the division between Latin and Greek Christians.

After the murder of his legate Peter of Castelnau in 1208, Innocent called a crusade against the Cathars of southern France. The Albigensian Crusade became a long and brutal war in which northern French lords seized southern lands, an outcome far from the conversion Innocent had hoped for.

sections.h2: Francis, Dominic and the Fourth Lateran Council
paras: Around 1209 or 1210 Innocent gave oral approval to the simple rule of life presented by St. Francis of Assisi and his first companions, and he also encouraged St. Dominic's preaching mission. In November 1215 he opened the Fourth Lateran Council, counted as the twelfth ecumenical council and attended by hundreds of bishops and abbots.

Its seventy-one canons opened with a profession of faith that used the term transubstantiation for the Eucharist. Canon 21 required every Catholic who has reached the age of discretion to confess at least once a year and receive Communion at least at Easter, a precept still in force. Other canons forbade clergy to take part in trials by ordeal, restricted the founding of new religious rules, regulated preaching and clerical education, and required Jews and Muslims to wear distinctive dress. Innocent died at Perugia on July 16, 1216, while preparing a new crusade.

keyFacts: Born Lotario dei Conti di Segni at Gavignano around 1160
Placed England under interdict (1208) and annulled Magna Carta (1215)
Called the Fourth Crusade, which sacked Constantinople in 1204
Approved St. Francis's way of life around 1209–1210

faqs.question: What did the Fourth Lateran Council teach?
faqs.answer: It professed the Catholic faith using the term transubstantiation, required annual confession and Easter Communion, reformed clerical life, forbade clergy to take part in ordeals and restricted new religious rules, among its seventy-one canons.

faqs.question: Did Innocent III approve the sack of Constantinople?
faqs.answer: No. He had excommunicated the crusaders for attacking Zara and condemned the violence of 1204, though he later accepted the Latin Empire established there.

faqs.question: Why did Innocent III annul Magna Carta?
faqs.answer: King John had made England a papal fief in 1213, and Innocent viewed the charter as extorted from his vassal by force, so he declared it void in 1215.
